widget_map.full_view: New route /app/guide (page title 'Guide'). Reachable from the Account menu, the phone 'More' sheet, the 'Help & guide' card on /app/settings and the step-12 copy. It renders every step of the crew guide as an ordinary scrollable document: one section per step with the same title, body, actions list and 'Try it:' text. Each section links to that widget's full page (/app/routines, /app/consents, /app/report, /app/report/privacy, /app/rewards, /app/rewards/activity, /app/insights). It also shows the user's progress ('Not started', 'In progress · step 5 of 12', 'Completed 7 Oct 2026', 'Skipped 7 Oct 2026'), a 'Start the live guide' button that opens the overlay on /app at step 1, and a 'What changed' note when the guide version is newer than the one the user finished. Compared with the card, the page does not depend on positions, so it works on phones, with screen readers, when widgets are hidden and in print. It is also the accessible fallback for the hover-only action rows.

widget_map.conflicts: Three alternative stores were rejected. (1) Storing progress on public.users: authenticated may update only (full_name, gender, operational_category, team). Worse, the users_select and users_update policies let an org admin read and update their crew's rows, so an org admin would see and could reset an individual's onboarding state. That breaks the rule that org admins see aggregates only. (2) A column on user_preferences_and_consent: RLS is right (owner only), but it mixes privacy consent with UI state, and savePreferences upserts the whole preference payload, so a guide column would have to be excluded from that upsert. (3) localStorage or cookie: does not follow the user across devices, and is lost on a shared crew-room device or after clearing site data. A dedicated table avoids all three problems.
widget_map.implementation_notes: Migration supabase/migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX_guide_progress.sql: create the table and the trigger set_updated_at → private.set_updated_at(); enable row level security. Then 'revoke all on public.user_guide_progress from anon, authenticated' (repeat the lockdown explicitly, per the project rule); grant select, insert, update to authenticated; grant all to service_role. Policies: guide_select for select to authenticated using (user_id = (select auth.uid())); guide_insert with check (user_id = (select auth.uid())); guide_update using and with check (user_id = (select auth.uid())). Deliberately no delete policy and no org-admin or super-admin read policy. Grant update on the whole table, not column-level: PostgREST upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) needs update on every supplied column, and RLS with check already pins user_id. Server action saveGuideProgress(event: 'open' | 'step' | 'skip' | 'finish', step, version), Zod GuideProgressInput in src/lib/schemas.ts, assertRole('end_user','org_admin','super_admin'), upsert with the RLS client, fire-and-forget from the client through startTransition; debounce 'step' events by about 600ms. Status rules: 'open' sets in_progress, increments open_count and sets last_opened_at. 'finish' sets completed and completed_at. 'skip' sets skipped and skipped_at. Esc counts as skip. Auto-open rules (evaluated in src/app/app/layout.tsx, which already queries per request; one PK lookup): open automatically on /app only when no row exists AND the user is new (users.created_at after the release date, or zero routine_sessions). Existing users instead get a one-time non-blocking pill 'New: a 2-minute guide to your dashboard'. If status is in_progress and the user left mid-tour, show a 'Guide paused · step N · Resume' pill on /app and other /app/* pages rather than re-opening over their work. When GUIDE_VERSION > guide_version and status is completed, offer 'What’s new' (changed steps only); never re-open for skipped users. Optional aggregate for org admins: add 'guide': {completed, skipped, in_progress, never_opened} counts for the org's end_users inside public.org_engagement_stats(); that keeps admins at aggregates only. Optional reward: a gamification_rules row ('guide_completed', 'Finish the dashboard guide', 10, 'once', 1) awarded through awardCredits on 'finish'. The once-only cooldown in admin_award_credits makes it tamper-proof even though the progress row is user-writable. This is a product decision; the default is no credits. Add scripts/rls-check.mjs cases: Dana cannot select, insert or update Yoav's row; the org admin selects 0 crew rows; anon gets an error. Regenerate types with npm run db:types, never by redirecting supabase gen types.

Table public.user_guide_progress: (user_id uuid not null references public.users(id) on delete cascade; guide_key text not null check (guide_key in ('crew_canvas','admin_canvas','super_canvas')); guide_version int not null default 1 check (guide_version between 1 and 1000); status text not null default 'in_progress' check (status in ('in_progress','completed','skipped')); current_step smallint not null default 0 check (current_step between 0 and 49); furthest_step smallint not null default 0 check (furthest_step between 0 and 49); open_count int not null default 1 check (open_count >= 0); first_opened_at, last_opened_at timestamptz not null default now(); completed_at, skipped_at timestamptz; updated_at timestamptz not null default now(); primary key (user_id, guide_key)). Trigger: before update → private.set_updated_at(). RLS enabled. Run 'revoke all on public.user_guide_progress from anon, authenticated' explicitly (project lockdown rule), then 'grant select, insert, update on public.user_guide_progress to authenticated' and 'grant all … to service_role'. Policies: guide_select (select, using user_id = (select auth.uid())), guide_insert (with check user_id = (select auth.uid())), guide_update (using and with check user_id = (select auth.uid())). No delete policy. No org-admin or super-admin row access. The grant is table-wide, not column-level, because PostgREST upsert needs update on every supplied column; RLS with check pins user_id. Code: src/lib/guide.ts loadGuideProgress(supabase, userId, key), GuideProgressInput (Zod) in src/lib/schemas.ts, and server action saveGuideProgress(event 'open'|'step'|'skip'|'finish', step, version) in src/app/app/actions.ts (assertRole all three roles; RLS client upsert; step events debounced client-side). Auto-open only for new users with no row; existing users get a one-time pill; skipped users are never re-opened; a newer GUIDE_VERSION offers 'What’s new' to completed users. risks: Accessibility of the card. The prototype card is an <aside> with no focus management, no keyboard support (no Esc, arrows or Enter), aria-hidden progress dots, and hover-only action rows (mouseenter/mouseleave on divs), so keyboard, screen-reader and touch users cannot follow it. Mitigation: role='dialog' aria-modal='false', an aria-live step announcement, row buttons with focus and click equivalents, visible 'Step N of M' text, and the /app/guide text version as a full fallback.

Accessibility of the spotlight and dim. The box-shadow ring disappears in Windows forced-colors mode. The 50% navy dim lowers contrast of everything not spotlit, and the user is told the app is 'fully usable underneath'. Use SVG strokes plus a forced-colors outline, and keep the dim pointer-events:none but never on top of modals.

Drag and resize accessibility (step 11 and the free slot). Drag-only movement violates WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7. Resize via S/M/L/XL must be a radio group. Every move needs a keyboard or single-pointer alternative with live announcements. If layouts ship without these, the guide teaches an inaccessible interaction.

Keyboard precedence clash. Esc already closes Modal and Drawer (useOverlay in overlays.tsx). The concept adds a left-bar 'Esc' (deselect), and the guide needs Esc to close. Define the order: open modal/drawer, then guide card focus, then widget selection.

Phones. No phone guide is designed. The concept's rule (full-width card, max 45vh, ignores the top-strip left bar) plus the sticky main bar, the phone context sheet and iOS safe areas can leave no visible canvas, and the prototype never scrolls targets into view. Dock the card as a bottom sheet, scroll targets into the upper half, never open the context sheet during the tour, and put 'Guide' in the 'More' sheet.

Navigation mid-tour. The dim is click-through, and several 'Try it:' instructions (step 5 Rules, step 6 'Open a session', step 9 Privacy) and links ('Continue to briefing', recent rows) leave /app. Without layout-level persistence and a resume pill the tour silently dies; with server writes it must not nag. Mount the GuideProvider in CrewShell and record in_progress.

Copy drift and false claims. The guide hardcodes '+10', '+20 credits', 'Week 41', '12 steps' and 'the two shown here', and makes claims that are untrue in the product: coaching as a crew routine, 'chosen for crews like yours', 'a number of days', 'Revoke', 'linked by your admin', and 'orange dot' vs the red dot. Super admins can change credits at /super/rules. Interpolate from gamification_rules and readiness_tiers, and have product and privacy review the anonymity-wall and consent statements.

Role variation. Org admins and super admins can open /app but cannot pair (end_user-only consent RLS and actions), and the seeded super admin has no organization (no rewards; StartRoutine fails with NO_ORGANIZATION). The step list must be role-filtered, or the guide will spotlight dead features.

Feature gating. Steps 1, 3 and 11 and the step-10 'Try it' teach move, resize, hide, add, arrange, reset, lock and drop, none of which exist yet. Shipping the guide before layouts would teach non-existent features. Gate the copy and steps on layoutFeaturesEnabled and renumber the dots.

Interruption. The board opens the tour on load. Auto-opening for every existing user at release would interrupt crews preparing for a flight or sim. Limit auto-open to new users; offer existing users a dismissible pill; never re-open after Skip.

Performance. The prototype keeps hover and selection state at the root and re-renders the entire canvas on every mouseenter, and runs getBoundingClientRect on several elements on every scroll and resize without throttling. In React with server-fed widgets, keep guide state isolated, toggle data attributes for highlights, rAF-throttle placement, and use ResizeObserver. The canvas adds per-load queries (scenario_context, outgoing consents, rewards, rules) and a service-role wall RPC for report status. Use a narrow status-only wall function and Promise.all, as page.tsx already does.

Write volume and integrity. Debounce progress writes per step and treat failures as non-fatal. Progress rows are user-writable, so never derive credits or permissions from them except through the once-only rule engine.

Stacking-context bugs. The concept relies on lifting targets to z 3 over a z 2 dim. Any transform, filter or contain on an ancestor (animations such as animate-sheet-in use transform) traps z-index and hides the spotlight. The SVG-mask approach avoids that, but the z tiers must still sit below Modal (z-40) so the redeem confirm and drawers work during the tour.

CSP. The current CSP allows inline style attributes ('unsafe-inline' in style-src) and only self-hosted images and fonts, so the guide's dynamic left/top and SVG mask are fine. The S3 logo must be self-hosted or inlined (img-src 'self' data: blob:). Never render step copy with dangerouslySetInnerHTML, especially if copy later becomes admin-authored. A future move to nonce-based styles would break inline style props unless placement switches to CSS variables set via CSSOM.

Privacy of onboarding data. Guide progress is personal behavioural data. Keep it owner-only (no org-admin row access), expose only org-level counts, and rely on on delete cascade for account deletion. Do not put step or status in URLs beyond the bare ?guide=1 trigger.

Design-system churn. The concept palette (ink #0E153E, action red #BD2025, hue 275) differs from the Sept 2026 tokens (blue --acc, orange warn) and uses one red for both primary actions and alerts (pending dot, 'Pending' pill), which risks colour-only meaning. It also defines no dark theme while the app ships one, so dark values for the dim, ring and card must be designed.

Internationalisation. The PRD is Hebrew. Placement candidates ('right of', 'left of'), the 'left bar' wording and the arrow-key mapping must mirror in RTL. The 96px label column in action rows may truncate translated labels.

Implementation stack. The project runs Next.js 16 with breaking changes (proxy.ts instead of middleware, async request APIs). Per AGENTS.md, consult node_modules/next/dist/docs before writing the provider, server actions and route handlers. Regenerate database.types.ts only through npm run db:types to avoid clobbering it.
